seoTitle: How to Create a Subdomain in Namecheap
metaDescription: Need a subdomain for a blog, app, or staging site? Learn how to add one in Namecheap's Advanced DNS settings and point it to the right server.
intro: A subdomain is a useful way to run a blog, app, or staging environment separately from your main site while staying under the same domain. This guide covers creating a subdomain in Namecheap using the Advanced DNS settings and pointing it to the correct destination.

steps.heading: Log in and open your Domain List
steps.body: Sign in to Namecheap and go to your Domain List to select the domain where you want to add the subdomain.

steps.heading: Access Advanced DNS settings
steps.body: Open the Advanced DNS tab for that domain, which is where individual DNS records including subdomains are managed.

steps.heading: Add a new subdomain record
steps.body: Create a new record, enter your desired subdomain name, and select the correct record type based on where it needs to point.

steps.heading: Set the correct IP or hosting target
steps.body: Point the record to a specific IP address or hosting server depending on whether the subdomain is for an app, blog, or staging site.

steps.heading: Test the subdomain after propagation
steps.body: Once DNS propagation completes, visit the subdomain to confirm it resolves correctly and works as intended worldwide.

faq.question: Do I need a separate hosting plan for a subdomain?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — a subdomain can point to the same hosting as your main domain or to a completely different server, depending on your setup.

faq.question: How long does it take for a new subdomain to work?
faq.answer: DNS propagation timing varies, so it's normal for a subdomain to take a little while before it resolves consistently worldwide.

faq.question: Can I use a subdomain for testing before launching?
faq.answer: Yes, subdomains are commonly used for staging environments so you can test changes before applying them to your live site.

faq.question: What record type should I use for a subdomain?
faq.answer: It depends on the destination — an A record points to an IP address, while a CNAME points to another domain name.
